title: Cross-language resilience defaults and stream-friendly idempotency key ergonomics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement cross-SDK default retry/backoff policies and an ergonomic idempotency key scheme optimized for streaming and non-streaming endpoints across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Provide concrete examples, migration path for customers, and tests that validate behavior under common failure modes.
background: Multiple customer and internal incidents have exposed inconsistent retry behavior across SDKs and poor streaming resume ergonomics when clients get transient errors mid-stream. Current repo-level patterns vary: some SDKs retry at the transport level, others at the request envelope level. We need consistent safety boundaries (which operations are retryable), convergent defaults, and explicit guidance for idempotency keys that work for large chat/stream workloads.
design_decisions: Default retry policy: exponential backoff with full jitter, initial_delay=200ms, multiplier=2.0, max_delay=5s, max_attempts=4
Retry window: per-request attempt timeout should be <= 1/2 of the overall operation timeout to make progress in streaming cases
Retryable error taxonomy: classify errors into RETRYABLE_TRANSIENT, RETRYABLE_THROTTLE, NON_RETRYABLE_CLIENT, NON_RETRYABLE_SERVER with examples and HTTP/gRPC mapping
Idempotency key format: adopt a short human-friendly prefix + base64 URL-safe 32-byte token; recommend optional semantic prefix for customers (e.g., 'rwd:conv:')

Streaming resume semantics: SDKs expose a Resume-Token header returned by the server on each chunk; SDKs should persist the latest token and include it on retry rather than resending whole prefix when possible
Safe defaults across languages: surface a single config object name (resilience) with same keys and shape in Python/TS/Go SDKs to reduce cross-language cognitive load

2026-03-05: Spike completed showing resume-token approach reduces duplicate tokens sent for 1k concurrent small-chat sessions (perf dashboard link in links).
2026-03-08: Internal review with security and API contracts — minor question on idempotency token entropy (security asked for 32-byte minimum).

acceptance_criteria: Each SDK (Python/TS/Go) implements a resilience config with identical key names and documented defaults
Retryable error taxonomy documented and linked from SDK docs; SDKs map transport errors to taxonomy accurately in tests
Idempotency key helper provided in each SDK that produces recommended tokens; examples for prefixed semantic keys included
Streaming SDKs persist and use server-provided resume tokens on retry; integration tests demonstrate resumed streams without duplicating already-received tokens
Performance/regression test: 0-3% tail-latency increase and <=5% token duplication in high-concurrency streaming workload compared to current baseline
PRs merged and release notes drafted for runtime-1.28 and sdk-2026.03 releases
code_examples:
Python (helper):
from redwood import Idempotency
key = Idempotency.create(prefix='rwd:conv', entropy_bytes=32)
# set in headers: {'Idempotency-Key': key}
# SDK will persist Resume-Token header on each chunk and use it on retry

Go (retry config):
cfg := redwood.ResilienceConfig{MaxAttempts:4, InitialDelay:200*time.Millisecond, MaxDelay:5*time.Second, Jitter: redwood.FullJitter}
client := redwood.NewClient(redwood.OptionResilience(cfg))
client.ChatStream(ctx, req)
notes: Trade-offs considered: aggressive retries reduce tail-latency but increase server-side load and duplicate tokens. We prefer conservative attempts (4) to balance cost and availability.

Idempotency design avoids pushing semantic parsing into the server; server treats idempotency key as opaque and best-effort. Customers with stronger semantics can layer their own metadata in request body.
Open question: whether to enable redirect-to-fallback-model retries automatically for certain error classes (proposal deferred to runtime routing team).
Follow-ups: add SDK linter rule to discourage naive use of infinite retry loops in user code; include examples in migration guide.
